proposed.explanation: Although the verified FY2025 top-line and balance sheet figures show operational growth, the provided evidence is insufficient for a responsible buy, hold, or sell recommendation. At the cutoff price of 141.95 EGP per share, your 300 shares of ETEL are worth 42,585.00 EGP alongside 20,000.00 EGP in cash, making a total portfolio of 62,585.00 EGP with 68.0% concentrated in a single stock. In FY2025, ETEL reported operating revenues of 106,672,946,000 EGP compared with 81,677,812,000 EGP in FY2024, representing 30.6% top-line growth. Gross profit increased by 47.0% from 30,492,762,000 EGP in FY2024 to 44,839,110,000 EGP in FY2025, expanding the gross margin from 37.3% to 42.0%. As of 31/12/2025, ETEL held total consolidated assets of 225,882,527,000 EGP against total consolidated equity of 63,687,826,000 EGP, implying total liabilities of 162,194,701,000 EGP. However, several critical items are missing: (1) bottom-line profitability (operating profit, financing costs, taxes, and net profit) to verify whether gross profit growth translated into net earnings despite high implied liabilities; (2) total issued shares or per-share metrics (EPS, book value per share, or market capitalization), without which the current 141.95 EGP share price cannot be valued; (3) cash flow statements, debt structure, and dividend information; and (4) any 2026 interim financial statements, as all available financial data ends on 31/12/2025 despite the 2026-11-18 cutoff. For a medium-risk, 5-7 year education savings goal already heavily concentrated in ETEL, deciding to add, hold, or sell without valuation, net earnings, cash flow, or recent 2026 performance would not be grounded in sufficient evidence. Note that all equity investments carry market and company-specific uncertainty, and this guidance is not a guarantee of returns.
